summary.one_liner: A Microsoft tutorial series for Python developers on building Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, centered on a Python study buddy app and an AI research paper learning server.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a tutorial series in three parts: setup and MCP core concepts, a Python Study Buddy console app backed by a custom MCP server, and an AI Research Learning MCP server. The study buddy covers prompts and basic tools, generating coding challenges and hints at beginner, intermediate, and expert levels. The research server is described with planned tools such as search_research_papers(), get_trending_papers(), create_study_plan(), summarize_paper(), track_learning_progress(), and send_research_learning(). The README also mentions storing daily research notes in a GitHub repo and links to arXiv and Papers With Code APIs. It points to a companion video and conference talk code.
use_cases: learn to build an MCP server in Python
build a Python study tutor with AI assistants
create an AI research paper search tool
generate study plans from research papers
example of prompts and tools in MCP
how_to_run: Install VS Code, Python 3.12+, and the Python extension
Follow Part 2 (Python Study Buddy) or Part 3 (AI Research Hub) in the README
notable: Two-part hands-on build: a study buddy app and a research server
Covers MCP prompts, basic tools, and resources in sequential parts
Companion to a YouTube walkthrough and an AI Engineer Paris talk
Links to a separate mcp-python-demo for a deeper getting-started guide
caveats: Requires Python 3.12 or later and VS Code setup
README does not describe the exact tool implementations or their current status; the research tools are listed as things you will build
